posts.cooked:
Hello everyone,

I need to apply a surcharge (extra charge or recargo) at the item level. Basically, the opposite of applying a discount at the item level. However, the key detail here is that I’m not allowed to change the item price (rate).
In other words:
Item Total = (Rate × Quantity) + Additional Charge

This should happen before taxes are applied. If the tax is inclusive, then additional calculations would be needed to adjust the item totals accordingly. The surcharge should apply both as a flat-surcharge and a percentage surcharge.

Invoice Totals:

  • Item1 Price: 250

  • Original subtotal: 9 × 250 = 2250

  • Surcharge (flat +150)

  • Net Item Total: 2400

  • Item2 Price: 150

  • Original subtotal: 10 × 150 = 1500

  • Surcharge (20% = +300)

  • Net Item Total: 1800

Summary:

  • Subtotal before surcharge: 2250 + 1500 = 3750
  • Surcharges applied: +150 (flat) +300 (20%) = +450
  • Net before tax: 4200
  • Tax (18%): 756
  • Grand Total: 4956

What I’m Looking For

  1. Is there a way in ERPNext to apply surcharges (extra charge or recargos) directly at the item level, just like discounts?
  2. I need support for both flat and percentage surcharges per line.
  3. Should this be implemented via client script, server script, or is there a recommended built-in feature?

Has anyone else come across this requirement? Any advice would be very helpful.

Thanks!

Hi Gary, you can already do this with the standard system without coding anything. Just use the Margin Type field in the item table under the Discount and Margin section. First, select the Margin Type: Percentage or Amount, and then enter the Margin Rate or Amount in the field above.

Note that you need to have an Item Price in the selected Price List for this to work. Also, be aware that if you select the wrong values, sometimes when you make changes the system does not recalculate, so it’s better to reload and enter the values correctly.

Hi @Malvin

Thank you very much for replying. I didn’t know this was an available feature, and I’m sure it will be helpful somehow. Unfortunately, this does not solve my problem, since this method changes the original item price (or item rate).

For example, if I apply a flat amount of $150 as a margin, the item price changes to $400, which significantly alters the final result. Therefore, the calculation would be: (250 + 150 margin) = 400 x 9 = 3600.

image1257×148 13.3 KB

However, my task is to apply a charge (or margin) that only affects the total at the item line level. Using the same example, the calculation would be: 250 x 9 = 2250 + 150 = 2400.

If you know of any solution, please let me know!
